events.text: The morning after the abdication you wake in the Palace of Tranquil Longevity, on the far side of the Forbidden City from the throne. Nobody comes to you with a memorial. At noon a eunuch you do not know brings a bowl of soup and a message from {sh_heir}: the new court would be honoured to hear the Retired Emperor's thoughts, when there are any.

choices.text: Send back word that there will be

effects.log: You fold the message small and keep it in your sleeve. {sh_He} will hear from you.

choices.text: Send back the soup bowl, empty, and nothing else

effects.log: Let {sh_heir} learn the throne alone for a season. You go and train in the old garden.

choices.text: Walk the long way round the palace, to be seen

effects.log: Ministers bow to you in the galleries as if nothing had changed. Everything has.

events.text: The hall on the back mountain is smaller than the head's quarters, and quieter. You hear the morning drill from here, faint, and {sh_heir}'s voice calling the forms where yours used to be. It is a little off the beat. Before noon two elders climb the path to tell you so, as if you could not hear it yourself.

choices.text: Tell them to go back and follow {sh_his} beat

effects.log: They go back down. The drill finds its rhythm by the end of the week.

choices.text: Tell them you will speak to {sh_him} about it

effects.log: They go down satisfied. Word gets round that the old head still has opinions.

choices.text: Close the door and sit down to cultivate

effects.log: Whatever is off the beat down there, it is not yours to count any more. You breathe.

events.text: At the first family dinner after the handing on, {sh_heir} sits in the head's chair and you sit at {sh_his} right hand. Halfway through the soup every face at the table turns to you before it turns to {sh_him}. You see {sh_heir} see it.

choices.text: Turn your own face to {sh_heir}, and wait

effects.log: The table follows your eyes. {sh_heir} lets out a breath and speaks.

choices.text: Answer the question yourself, kindly

effects.log: They listen to you, as they always have. {sh_heir} eats the rest of the meal in silence.

choices.text: Excuse yourself before the second course

effects.log: You walk out into the courtyard and leave the table to its new head.

events.text: A rider comes up from the Ministry of War with the heir's seal and a map. The northern border lords are raiding again, and {sh_heir} means to send forty thousand men across the river in spring. The Ministry wants to know if the Retired Emperor approves. Behind the question is another one: whose army it is.

choices.text: Send back your seal beside {sh_his}: the war has your blessing

effects.log: The army marches under one name. The court likes that.

choices.text: Forbid the crossing: an envoy first, then the sword

effects.log: You write it in your own hand. The army stays on its side of the river, and {sh_heir} reads your letter twice.

choices.text: Send the map back unmarked

effects.log: The Ministry takes your silence as it likes. {sh_heir} marches. Nobody asks you how it went.

events.text: The Board of Rites has a match for {sh_heir}: a royal of the western empire, with a dowry of horses and a peace treaty folded inside it. The Empress Dowager's faction wants a child of their own house instead. Both sides have sent you presents. Both are waiting to see which present you keep.

choices.text: Tell the Board it is {sh_heir}'s choice and {sh_his} alone

effects.log: You return both presents. {sh_heir} chooses, and remembers that you let {sh_him}.

choices.text: Choose for {sh_him}: the treaty, the horses, the west

effects.log: The match is made on your word. The wedding is splendid. {sh_heir} smiles through all of it like a prisoner at a sentencing.

choices.text: Keep both presents and say nothing

effects.log: Two factions read two meanings into your silence and fight about it all winter.

events.text: A list arrives in a lacquered box: eleven ministers {sh_heir} believes are plotting, and the evidence against them, some of it good. The Censorate asks whether the Retired Emperor will sign beside the new Emperor's seal. Three of the names served you for thirty years.

choices.text: Sign beside {sh_his} seal

effects.log: The purge is swift and the court is quiet after. Some of the quiet is fear.

choices.text: Strike out the three names you know, and send it back

effects.log: Eight are dismissed. Three are spared on your word. {sh_heir} does not forget whose word.

choices.text: Close the box and send it back unopened

effects.log: The purge goes ahead without your name on it. You sleep badly, and it is your own business why.

events.text: The Grand Secretariat has split in two over the salt monopoly, and both halves have come to your palace by different gates on the same afternoon. The younger ministers stand with {sh_heir}. The older ones stand with you, or say they do. Either way the court cannot move until someone says which half is the court.

choices.text: Receive the younger ministers first, and send them back with your support

effects.log: The old guard goes home without an audience. They understand.

choices.text: Receive the old guard, and send the heir a list of terms

effects.log: The salt monopoly is settled your way. Half the court thanks you. The other half reports every word to {sh_heir}.

choices.text: Receive neither: you are at your cultivation

effects.log: Both halves wait at your gates until dusk and go away. The court stays split.

events.text: The war {sh_heir} began has gone badly. A general writes to you privately: the heir will not hear of retreat, and the men are eating their horses. He asks you to order them home over the new Emperor's head.

choices.text: Tell the general to obey his Emperor

effects.log: He obeys. Some of his men come home in the spring, and the court calls it a victory.

choices.text: Order the army home in your own name

effects.log: The army comes home. The general is grateful. {sh_heir} is not.

choices.text: Burn the letter

effects.log: You do not answer, and the general does what generals do without orders.

events.text: {sh_heir} climbs the back mountain path in person, which {sh_he} has not done in a year. A rival sect has insulted {sh_house} at the Martial Alliance and {sh_he} wants to call the disciples to arms. {sh_He} says it is to ask your advice. {sh_He} has already sent for the armoury keys.

choices.text: Tell {sh_him} a head must answer an insult

effects.log: {sh_He} goes down the mountain lighter. You hear the war drums the next morning.

choices.text: Forbid it: a feud of words is not worth one disciple

effects.log: You say it plainly, and the elders hear you say it. The drums stay silent. {sh_heir} does not climb your path again for some time.

choices.text: Pour {sh_him} tea and talk about the weather

effects.log: {sh_He} drinks the tea and goes down none the wiser. The war goes ahead without you.

events.text: A boy has come to the gate of {sh_house} with demonic qi coiled in his meridians like a snake asleep. {sh_heir} wants to take him in and cure him. The elders want him driven off before the Alliance hears of it. They have all come up the mountain together, which has not happened since you held the seat.

choices.text: Stand with {sh_heir}: the boy stays

effects.log: The boy stays. The elders go down muttering. {sh_heir} bows lower to you than {sh_he} needs to.

choices.text: Overrule {sh_him}: the gate stays closed

effects.log: The boy is sent away with a little silver and a warning. {sh_heir} watches him go and says nothing to you at all.

choices.text: Tell them the seat is {sh_heir}'s and close your door

effects.log: They argue outside your door for an hour, and then go down to settle it without you.

events.text: The Martial Alliance asks every great sect to share one secret art with the others against the coming calamity. {sh_heir} would give them the third form of the sect's heart method. You wrote that form into the manual yourself, forty years ago, and nobody outside these walls has ever seen it.

choices.text: Let {sh_him} give it: the calamity is everyone's

effects.log: The form goes to the Alliance under the seal of {sh_house}. The murim thinks better of both of you.

choices.text: Forbid it: the third form stays in this hall

effects.log: You keep the manual on your own table now. {sh_heir} sends the Alliance something lesser, and an apology.

choices.text: Let {sh_heir} decide without you

effects.log: You do not ask what {sh_he} decided. You notice later that the manual is back on its shelf, and a page is missing.

events.text: A great house of the south offers a marriage alliance: their second son or daughter for the eldest grandchild of {sh_house}. {sh_heir} is for it. The match would bring silver and an old grudge with it. The matchmaker has been told to wait for the elder of the house before anyone signs.

choices.text: Tell the matchmaker the head has spoken

effects.log: The alliance is signed under {sh_heir}'s name. The grudge comes along with the silver, as you knew it would.

choices.text: Refuse the match yourself

effects.log: The matchmaker leaves without a signature. {sh_heir} hears it from a servant before {sh_he} hears it from you.

choices.text: Tell the matchmaker you are too old for weddings

effects.log: The matchmaker looks at {sh_heir}. {sh_heir} looks at the door you went out of, and signs.

events.text: The eastern branch of {sh_house} has stopped sending its rents and started calling its own head "Patriarch". {sh_heir} wants to ride east with the household guard. The branch has written to you instead: they will kneel to the old head, they say, but not to the new one.

choices.text: Send their letter on to {sh_heir} unopened

effects.log: They have their answer. {sh_heir} rides east with your letter in {sh_his} sleeve and the branch kneels within the month.

choices.text: Ride east yourself and take their oath to you

effects.log: The branch kneels to you at the gate. You make them swear to {sh_heir} too. They swear the way people swear when someone is watching.

choices.text: Let the head and the branch settle it

effects.log: It takes two years and some broken heads. The branch comes back in the end, and does not thank you for anything.

events.text: The house is short of silver after the floods, and {sh_heir} means to sell the old orchard below the ancestral graves to a salt merchant. The steward has brought the deed for your mark, because the oldest graves of the line lie there, and yours will lie beside them.

choices.text: Put your mark beside {sh_his}

effects.log: The orchard is sold. The silver gets the house through the winter. You visit the graves one more time, alone.

choices.text: Refuse, and pay the shortfall from your own share

effects.log: The orchard stays the family's. {sh_heir} is grateful in public, and in private does the sums of how much of the house is still yours.

choices.text: Tell the steward the dead do not need an orchard

effects.log: The steward takes the deed back down the hill. The salt merchant plants mulberries.

events.text: You are woken at the hour of the ox by torches in the courtyard of the Palace of Tranquil Longevity. The guard at your door is not your guard. A eunuch reads out an edict in {sh_heir}'s name: for the Retired Emperor's health, a palace has been made ready in a far province, and the carriage is waiting now.

choices.text: Get into the carriage

effects.log: You go. The road south is long and the escort is very polite.

choices.text: Walk past the guard to the Hall of Supreme Harmony, and call {sh_heir} out

effects.log: Nobody quite dares to stop you. By dawn the whole court is watching two emperors on the same steps.

choices.text: Send the eunuch back with one line: "Come and say it to my face"

effects.log: An hour later {sh_heir} comes, alone, with no guard. The two of you sit down.

events.text: Your share of the treasury has not come this quarter, and when your steward asks, the Ministry has no record of it. Then the old ministers who visit you are arrested one by one. Then the gate of your palace is bricked up on the outside, all but one door, and the door is watched. {sh_heir} has decided there is one emperor too many.

choices.text: Accept it: an old sovereign does not war on {sh_his} own heir

effects.log: You send word that you will go wherever the court thinks best.

choices.text: Break out through the bricked gate and go to the Hall

effects.log: The bricks were laid in a hurry. You walk out through them in the middle of the day.

choices.text: Write to {sh_heir} with your own brush: what is it {sh_he} fears

effects.log: The letter goes out by the watched door. An answer comes back in {sh_his} hand.

events.text: The elders climb the back mountain in a body, and this time {sh_heir} is not with them. They bring the head's order on a jade slip: for the peace of {sh_house}, the Grand Elder will keep to the back mountain in seclusion, see no disciples and send no letters. The order has {sh_heir}'s seal and, under it, the seals of most of the council.

choices.text: Bow, and go into seclusion

effects.log: You accept the slip with both hands. The path down the mountain is closed behind them.

choices.text: Go down the mountain and take the seal back

effects.log: You walk down past the elders and through the main gate. The disciples in the yard stop their forms to watch.

choices.text: Ask the elders to bring {sh_heir} up, and talk

effects.log: They look at each other. One of them goes down, and comes back up with {sh_heir} behind him.

events.text: {sh_heir} has told the Martial Alliance that the old head of {sh_house} is ill in the mind, and that nothing said in the Grand Elder's name speaks for the sect. A disciple who still loves you brings the letter up the mountain in tears.

choices.text: Let it stand: the sect is {sh_his} now

effects.log: You burn the letter and thank the disciple. Let the murim think what it likes.

choices.text: Go down and show the main hall how ill you are

effects.log: You go down the mountain with your sword. The main hall clears very quickly.

choices.text: Go down unarmed and ask {sh_heir} why

effects.log: You go down with empty hands. {sh_heir} sees them, and sends the guards out of the hall.

events.text: The elders of {sh_house} have been called to the ancestral hall without you. You hear of it from the gatekeeper. When you arrive {sh_heir} is in the head's chair, and {sh_he} is telling them that a house cannot have two heads, and that one of them must be laid in the ancestral tablets early, as an honour.

choices.text: Bow to the tablets and leave the council

effects.log: You bow to the tablets, and to {sh_heir}, and walk out. Half the hall stands up as you go.

choices.text: Stand before the tablets and ask the elders to choose

effects.log: You stand under the names of the dead. The elders look from you to the chair, and back.

choices.text: Kneel beside {sh_heir} before the tablets, and speak to {sh_him} alone

effects.log: The elders go out to wait in the courtyard. The incense burns down twice.

events.text: A cousin tells you over wine that {sh_heir} has stopped your share of the rents, moved your rooms to the old wing and told the servants to bring your meals cold. "The house is tired of being asked twice," the cousin says, and then, more quietly: "Half the elders would follow you out of the gate."

choices.text: Tell the cousin you are content in the old wing

effects.log: You eat your cold meals and say nothing. The house stops asking you anything.

choices.text: Call the elders to the hall and make them choose

effects.log: The cousin smiles and goes to fetch them. The courtyard is full by evening.

choices.text: Go to {sh_heir}'s rooms tonight, alone

effects.log: You knock on the door of the head's rooms, as a guest knocks.

events.text: You send the last of your seals to {sh_heir} wrapped in yellow silk, with no letter. In the afternoon {sh_heir} comes to the Palace of Tranquil Longevity without an escort and sits with you in the garden, and for a long time neither of you says anything about the court at all.

choices.text: Tell {sh_him} about your own first year on the throne

effects.log: {sh_He} listens as {sh_he} has not listened since {sh_he} was a child. When {sh_he} goes, {sh_he} goes lighter.

choices.text: Say only: "It is yours. I will not be asked again."

effects.log: {sh_He} bows to you as an emperor bows to no one, and goes back to {sh_house}.

choices.text: Show {sh_him} the garden instead

effects.log: You walk the paths until the lanterns are lit. It is the best afternoon either of you has had in years.

events.text: You carry the last of your jade slips down the mountain yourself and lay them on the head's table in front of {sh_heir}. "The seat does not need my shadow," you say. "It never did." The disciples in the yard pretend not to hear.

choices.text: Walk back up the mountain without looking round

effects.log: You do not look round. Behind you {sh_heir} calls the forms, exactly on the beat.

choices.text: Stay for the evening drill, at the back of the yard

effects.log: You stand among the youngest disciples and follow {sh_heir}'s count like one of them.

choices.text: Give {sh_heir} your old sword-cord for luck

effects.log: {sh_He} ties it on {sh_his} own hilt. You will see it at every gathering of {sh_house} after.

events.text: At the next family dinner you take the lowest seat at the table, below the youngest cousin. When the soup comes the faces still turn to you out of habit. You turn yours to {sh_heir}, and keep it there, until they learn.

choices.text: Raise your cup to the head of the house

effects.log: The whole table raises its cups. {sh_heir} has to look away for a moment.

choices.text: Tell the children a story of the founders instead

effects.log: The children forget the head is at the table. So, for an evening, does the head.

choices.text: Leave early, and leave the table its head

effects.log: You walk out into the courtyard. Behind you the house carries on talking, and does not wait for you.
